subject: Dedicated capacity options and phased onramp — LynxBio
messages:
From: Kelly Park <kelly@lynxbio.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: Dr. Omar Ruiz <omar.ruiz@lynxbio.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing guidance and timelines

Connor —

Thanks for the quick conversation yesterday. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for an internal genomics inference workload (long context sequence scoring, lots of small requests plus periodic batch jobs). Before we get the procurement team involved, could you send a couple of concrete reservation options with: cluster footprint (GPU count), minimum guaranteed GPUs, suggested ramp schedule (pilot -> steady-state), and any notes on burst/bypass behavior and cost buckets?

High-level constraints from our side:
- Target latency: p95 < 200ms for single inference on 4k tokens (where realistic)
- Estimated steady token volume: ~120M tokens/day in 6 months
- Procurement prefers a phased spend over 6 months, not a single large commit

Appreciate a simple table and a recommended path. Happy for a short call if helpful.

—Kelly
Kelly Park
Head of AI Platforms | LynxBio
kelly@lynxbio.com

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Kelly Park <kelly@lynxbio.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing guidance and timelines

Kelly —

Thanks — putting a concise set of reservation options together below. I built these to balance predictable cost with the ability to scale quickly if you spike (burst lanes + autoscale). Attached: "LynxBio_Dedicated_Offer_Connor_v2.pdf" and draft SOW.

Summary (recommendation at the end):

Option 1 — Pilot-first (low commitment)
- Baseline cluster: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (min guaranteed 6)
- Use case: validate model integration and KV/prefix caching, early performance tuning
- Ramp: 0–4 weeks pilot; expand to 16 GPUs if pilot metrics good (month 2)
- Burst: allow up to 24 GPUs for short windows (on-demand burst pool)
- Pros: lowest initial monthly commit; minimal risk
- Cons: higher token unit cost at scale

Option 2 — Phased Reserved (recommended)
- Baseline cluster: 24 A100-eq GPUs (min guaranteed 18)
- Use case: production inference with predictable throughput and reserve lanes for batch windows
- Ramp schedule: Week 0 pilot on 8 GPUs (QA & perf tuning) -> Month 1 to 16 GPUs -> Month 3 to 24 GPUs steady-state
- Burst: +24 GPUs available for scheduled batch windows (billing at burst rate)
- Pros: predictable unit economics, smoother cost curve, meets p95 latency targets with batching/KV caching
- Cons: moderate upfront commit

Option 3 — High-commit (throughput optimized)
- Baseline cluster: 48 A100-eq GPUs (min guaranteed 40)
- Use case: high throughput, low per-token cost at scale
- Ramp: phased activation over 3 months to reach baseline
- Burst: managed across regions if needed
- Pros: best unit cost; strong SLA options
- Cons: highest monthly commit; procurement heavier lift

Notes on latency and architecture:
- For your 4k token p95 goal we recommend a mix of 16-bit quantized transformer kernels plus longer token optimized kernels; karthik (cc'd) can validate model-specific kernel selections, which impacts the minimum GPU footprint.
- We enable automatic KV cache + prefix caching to reduce repeated computation for multi-turn sequences; this typically reduces effective token load by 15–30% after warmup.
- Autoscale settings can be tuned to maintain p95 targets while keeping cost under control; we recommend a soft ceiling for bursts and scheduled batch lanes to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

Recommended path (my pick): Option 2 — Phased Reserved. Start pilot on 8 GPUs (prove infra + eval), commit to a 24-GPU lane by month 3 once QA targets are met. This aligns with procurement's phased spend preference and gives predictable economics while allowing for controlled bursts for batch work.

Next steps:
1) I'll attach a short offer + SOW (attached) and a proposed timeline.
2) If that looks good, we can open a DocuSign envelope and loop procurement — I included a placeholder DocuSign link in the attachments.
3) Karithik can run a short perf validation run with a small sample set to confirm the 24-GPU footprint meets your p95 target.

Available for a 30-minute call Wed/Thu if you want to walk the schedule.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Attachments: LynxBio_Dedicated_Offer_Connor_v2.pdf (application/pdf), SOW_LynxBio_PhasedOnramp.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing guidance and timelines

Connor — quick technical notes to include in the offer before we send to procurement: 

1) Sequence length sensitivity: If Lynx uses sustained 4k tokens frequently, the effective throughput per GPU drops ~25% compared to 2k sequences. Recommend we size Option 2's minimum guaranteed to 20 GPUs instead of 18 to preserve p95 headroom. We should also include an explicit warmup period and expected KV cache hit-rate assumptions in the SOW.

2) Quantization profile: For heavy batch jobs we recommend enabling int8 for batch transforms (saves ~2.5x memory) but keep fp16 for latency-sensitive single-request paths. Add an appendix outlining when we flip profiles.

3) Activation cadence: For procurement comfort, split the 24-GPU commitment into two 12-GPU tranches with clear activation triggers (metrics-based). That often eases internal CAPEX approvals.

I'll attach a short perf checklist we can drop in the SOW. Marissa — can you confirm the SLA credit language for the phased activation?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Kelly Park <kelly@lynxbio.com>, procurement@lynxbio.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing guidance and timelines

Kelly / Procurement team —

Per Karthik's feedback I've adjusted the recommended reservation path to make the procurement handoff smoother. Key changes shown below; full details are in the attached SOW and offer (same file names as before).

Revised recommended path (final):
- Phase A (Pilot): 8 GPUs active immediately for integration & perf validation (min guaranteed 6). Expected 2–4 week runway.
- Phase B (Initial reserved tranche): activate 12 GPUs (min guaranteed 10) at start of Month 2 once pilot acceptance criteria met.
- Phase C (Full reserved lane): expand to a 24-GPU steady lane (min guaranteed 20) by the start of Month 3 after successful batch validation.
- Burst lanes: additional +24 GPUs available for scheduled batch windows; burst billing applies.

Commercial notes:
- We will present a two-tranche commitment schedule to match procurement preferences (tranche activation tied to acceptance metrics in the SOW).
- DocuSign link for initial offer is ready: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/LYNX-BIO-OFFER-20270305
- Requested PO timeline: procurement confirmation + PO within 21 days of SOW signature to align GPU activation windows.

Practical risk mitigations:
- We include a one-time performance remediation window (two weeks) post-activation if p95 targets aren't met; remediation steps and credit language captured in SOW.
- We'll run a 24–48 hour runbook with your infra team during Phase B activation to reduce cold-start impact and prime KV caches.

Please let me know if procurement has preferred billing milestones and we can reflect those. If this works, I'll issue the DocuSign envelope and copy in our finance lead for invoicing terms.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Attachments: LynxBio_Dedicated_Offer_Connor_v2.pdf (application/pdf), SOW_LynxBio_PhasedOnramp.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Connor —

Thanks — the phased approach looks good and aligns with internal approvals. Procurement, please review the SOW and confirm whether we need any additional credit language for the performance remediation window.

Tentatively we want to proceed with the revised Phase B/C path (tranches to 12 -> 24 GPUs) assuming the SOW finalizes the activation triggers. Can Connor / Redwood confirm PO payment terms (Net 45?) and whether we can push the first tranche activation to the start of April to align with budget cycles.

I'll wait for procurement notes and sign-off.

—Kelly

Head of AI Platforms | LynxBio
kelly@lynxbio.com
